note: The agent registry. Nano Foundry's three agents are declared here — tools, model, instructions and limits — rather than hand-wired into code paths. The Python service (py/service.py) and the browser both read this file, so changing a model or a limit is a config change, not a code change. Every run writes a trace, and any trace can be replayed. See docs/tracks.md.

catalogue.list.description: The fixed 40-entry catalogue, ids and actions only. Read-only; there is no write tool and no upload tool anywhere in this registry.

lane.validate.description: Run a proposed lane through the symbolic molecule model and the four team checks. This is what decides whether a lane works — not the model.

splice.funnel.description: Enumerate candidate splice points for a pair and run the six hard-reject filters over each.

filters.explain.description: Return the deterministic reason string a filter already produced, for the explainer to put into plain words.

sources.search.description: The one retrieval path in the app. Holds the SerpApi key server-side and returns public references for a catalogue card or for a failure mode a filter has already named. Results are screened against the topics docs/scope.md §1 excludes before they leave the server; there is no second retrieval path and no write path.

events.write.description: Append a time-series row to the event store (Timescale hypertable, or the JSONL buffer when no database is configured).

agents.title: Pipeline builder
agents.job: Turn a sentence of English into a candidate lane of catalogue enzymes.
guarantees: Every enzyme id it returns is checked against the fixed catalogue and dropped if it is not there.
It proposes a lane; whether that lane runs is decided by lane.validate, which is deterministic code.

agents.title: Rejection explainer
agents.job: Put a deterministic filter verdict into plain English for a student.
guarantees: It never decides a verdict; it receives one and rewords it.
If it is unavailable the UI falls back to the filter's own wording, which is always present.

agents.title: Literature explainer
agents.job: Read references retrieved about the failure mode a filter already named, and say what they report.
guarantees: It is handed a verdict and a list of retrieved references; it never decides a verdict and never scores anything.
It sees only the screened reference titles and snippets plus the filter's own reason, so it has nothing else to draw a number from.
If it is unavailable the panel still shows the references and the filter's own wording, which are both present without it.

agents.title: Filter sweep runner
agents.job: Walk catalogue pairs, run the funnel over every candidate, and write each verdict to the event store.
guarantees: No model is involved at all, which is why its output is reproducible and testable.
It is declared here anyway so the platform treats deterministic workers and model-backed agents the same way.
